note: Passage 3707 (Pro 1:11) — the wicked's plot: 'let us ambush the innocent without reason.' 'innocent' (naqi) read as the guiltless moral state, from the victim's side (no valence-filtering of the malice around it).

dims.v: the innocent — the guiltless one, blameless of any provocation
the innocent standing guiltless, made the object of an unprovoked ambush
paired with 'without reason' (chinnam) — innocence stressed by the lack of any cause

naqi is the moral state of the VICTIM — guiltlessness — surfaced only to be violated 'without reason'. The read holds the innocence as a real inner state, not merely a plot-detail; the wickedness is that it targets the blameless.
